cards.explanation: The answer is to shout for joy and sing. The LORD's very first words are: “Shout for joy, O barren woman, who bears no children; break forth in song and cry aloud…” Notice He doesn't say "hold it together." He says CRY ALOUD. I think that's a woman who just got permission to be as loud as she wants.

The answer is True, and that's the surprising part. The LORD says “…more are the children of the desolate woman than of her who has a husband…” You'd expect the numbers to go the other way, friends. I think that's why it lands so hard.

The answer is to make it bigger, friends, and bigger is the whole assignment. The LORD says, “Enlarge the site of your tent, stretch out the curtains of your dwellings, do not hold back.” Then He adds, “Lengthen your ropes and drive your stakes in deep.” That's a woman being told to stop being modest about her floor plan.

The reason is that she will spread out to the right and left. The LORD says, “For you will spread out to the right and left…” Her descendants will also “…dispossess the nations and inhabit the desolate cities.” So the tent grows because the family does. That's a lot of folding chairs.

The answer is False. The LORD says she won't carry it: “For you will forget the shame of your youth and will remember no more the reproach of your widowhood.” Forget it. Remember it no more. I think that's one heavy bag finally set down.

Her Maker, friends! The LORD says, “For your husband is your Maker…” and He names Himself the LORD of Hosts. The very One who made her is the One who stands by her. I did NOT see that coming the first time.

The word is deserted. The LORD says, “…like a wife deserted and wounded in spirit, like the rejected wife of one’s youth…” It's a hurting picture, friends. And He's the One saying He has called her back.

He says it was for a brief moment. The LORD says, “For a brief moment I forsook you, but with great compassion I will bring you back.” Compare that moment to the great compassion coming after. It's a small moment next to a big promise.

The answer is False, because the moment belongs to the hiding. The LORD says, “In a surge of anger I hid My face from you for a moment, but with everlasting kindness I will have compassion on you…” Everlasting means everlasting, friends. That's the one that sticks around.

The LORD swore that the waters would never again cover the earth. He says, “…I swore that the waters of Noah would never again cover the earth.” Noah is the man who entered the ark before the floodwaters came (Genesis 7:7). Then He says, “…I have sworn that I will not be angry with you or rebuke you.”

The answer is True, and He puts it in the strongest picture around. He says, “Though the mountains may be removed and the hills may be shaken, My loving devotion will not depart from you, and My covenant of peace will not be broken…” The mountains may be removed, friends, but His covenant of peace will not be broken.

He builds the city out of precious stones and jewels! Stones set in antimony, foundations of sapphires, pinnacles of rubies, gates of sparkling jewels, “…and all your walls of precious stones.” Not one thing in this build is ordinary. Somebody's getting the nicest address in the whole book.
The answer is False. The LORD says, “Then all your sons will be taught by the LORD…” All, friends, not just a few. And He adds, “…great will be their prosperity.”

Terror will not come near her. The LORD says, “Terror will be far removed, for it will not come near you.” Right before that He says, “…you will have no fear.” Terror doesn't even get close enough to knock.

They will fall before her. The LORD says, “If anyone attacks you, it is not from Me; whoever assails you will fall before you.” He says an attack on her is not from Him. And whoever assails her is the one who falls before her.

The answer is True. The LORD says, “Behold, I have created the craftsman who fans the coals into flame and forges a weapon fit for its task…” He made the one at the forge. I think that's one of the biggest things in the passage to chew on, friends.

The weapon will not prosper. The LORD says, “No weapon formed against you shall prosper…” The weapon can be made, but it doesn't win. And He goes on to say she will refute every tongue that accuses her.

It's the heritage of the servants of the LORD. He says, “This is the heritage of the servants of the LORD, and their vindication is from Me…” declares the LORD. That comes right after He says no weapon formed against her will prosper. He wraps it all up by naming who it's for, friends. It's for His servants.

It comes from the LORD Himself. He says, “…their vindication is from Me…” declares the LORD. It doesn't come from their strength or their name, friends. It comes from Him, and you can't hand that job to anybody else.
